title: HotelBooking flow maps
lede: One page per promoted hypothesis. Each maps every screen, branch and failure path, with every transition tagged by the acceptance criterion it satisfies.

hotel pins (map mode) — same underlying result set

transitions.trigger: guest applies or changes a filter/sort chip

nodes.label: [Handoff] Room Detail

flows.title: Flow map — HYP-002: Live room-detail re-price & availability

nodes.label: Room Detail
regions: flat info stack (description, occupancy limits, amenities, hotel policies)
booking form: date-range field, per-room occupancy stepper
extras/add-ons section (conditional — omitted entirely if none configured, AC-1.12)
price/availability area (loading / error / normal states layer here — see nodes 3, 5, 6)
Book Now / Add to Cart CTA (disabled while unavailable or invalid)

transitions.ac: AC-1.6 (picker itself restricts selectable dates to the hotel's booking window — see § 3 note)

transitions.trigger: guest taps Book Now / Add to Cart (enabled only when available)
transitions.ac: AC-1.1/1.2 happy path, hands off to HYP-003

decision.question: Does the edited occupancy stay within max_adults / max_children / max_guests?

outcomes.label: No
outcomes.note: inline validation error naming which limit was exceeded; CTA disabled; no recomputation fired (client-side, no network round-trip, AC-1.3)

transitions.trigger: OPEN CHOICE (a): auto-extend checkout date, inform guest
transitions.ac: AC-1.5 — tech-lead to pick (a) or (b), not both

transitions.trigger: OPEN CHOICE (b): block, inline minimum-nights message
transitions.ac: AC-1.5 — tech-lead to pick (a) or (b), not both

decision.question: Does the guest's selected date range satisfy the room type's min_los?

nodes.label: Debounced Recomputation
nodes.archetype_note: Not in the given archetype vocabulary (list/detail/form/dialog/confirmation/empty-state/error-state/map/gallery/split) — added because AC-1.1 makes a visible in-progress state an explicit requirement distinct from the resting screen. Flagging the addition.
regions: price/availability area shows a loading indicator
rest of the screen (gallery, info stack) unchanged

transitions.note: discard silently — no UI change, the newer result governs what's displayed

transitions.trigger: this is the most recent request

What does the local AvailabilityEngine/PricingEngine return?

Book Now / Add to Cart CTA disabled

nodes.label: Only M Left

'notice' rather than 'error-state' because it's an actionable nudge (reduce quantity), not a failure.

nodes.label: [Handoff] Cart / DEC-008 check
nodes.note: Continues in HYP-003 flow map, node 0 — including the single-hotel-cart conflict check (AC-2.11).

decision.question: What does the inline live check return?

transitions.trigger: guest opens the full detail screen

nodes.label: Sheet: Only M Left

nodes.label: [N/A UNDER DEC-010] Network failure during re-price

nodes.note: AC-1.10, preserved not deleted per the coordinator's original instruction. Not reachable in the current local-only architecture — kept here as a disconnected/orphan node exactly as ba-requirements-review.md marks it, not wired into any live transition.

flows.bet: A live, native room-detail screen with instant re-price on date/occupancy change reduces late-stage 'unavailable' surprises and increases add-to-cart completion
notes: Behavior only, per DEC-019. AC ids below (AC-1.x) are the Given/When/Then criteria already sharpened in reviews/ba-requirements-review.md § 3.1 — this flow does not rewrite them, only sequences them.

flows.title: Flow map — HYP-003: Flat checkout + guest policy + simulated payment

transitions.trigger: cart already holds a room from a different hotel
no conflict — cart is empty or already single-hotel

decision.question: Does the cart already contain a room from a hotel other than the one being added?

nodes.label: Cart Conflict dialog
regions: "Your cart already has rooms from [Hotel A]. This version books one hotel at a time — clear your cart to search a different hotel?"
Clear cart and add this instead (primary action)

transitions.trigger: guest taps 'Clear cart and add this instead'
zero items in cart (deep link, expired session, or every line rejected at 3)

decision.question: Is the cart empty when checkout is entered?

nodes.label: Any cart line changed since added?

transitions.trigger: a line's price changed or availability dropped

decision.question: Does re-validating every cart line against the local AvailabilityEngine/PricingEngine find any change since the line was added?

nodes.label: Price/Availability Changed
regions: per-line old vs. new price, or "no longer available"

transitions.trigger: guest removes the now-unavailable line and the cart is now empty

nodes.label: Checkout Screen
regions: guest/account info fields (name, email, phone — no address fields)
"sign in instead" link (see § 3 Finding — destination undefined)
payment section — revealed only once a guest/account identity exists (AC-2.6)
within payment section once revealed: no card-shaped input fields, persistent "DEMO PAYMENT — NO REAL CHARGE" banner (non-dismissible), Simulate Payment action (AC-2.8)
sticky price summary: total booking value / due now / due later, shown distinctly (AC-2.7)

transitions.trigger: guest taps Simulate Payment (only reachable once identity exists)
missing required field or invalid email format

decision.question: Are all required guest-info fields present and valid?

outcomes.label: No
outcomes.note: inline field-level errors; payment not reachable until resolved

transitions.trigger: proceeds as guest — local guest identity row created, payment section reveals

transitions.ac: AC-2.5 names this option but does not define its destination — see § 3 Finding

decision.question: Does the guest proceed with guest info alone, or choose to sign in instead?

nodes.label: Sign In [FLOW GAP]
nodes.note: Not modeled further — see § 3 Findings. AC-2.5 preserves 'a sign in instead option remains available but is never forced' verbatim from the pre-DEC-010 spec, but no artifact defines what signing in means or does under a fully local, single-device, no-backend architecture with no defined login mechanism. Drawn as a labeled dead end, not invented.

nodes.label: Booking Confirmation
nodes.note: Cart is cleared on entry to this node (AC-2.10). A local notification fires here per DEC-013/booking-confirmation.md, replacing the reference's email confirmation — not modeled as a separate node since it's a system side-effect, not a screen.

nodes.label: [N/A UNDER DEC-011] Payment failure
regions: retry-capable decline/error state (preserved spec, not built)
nodes.note: Original AC-2.8, retired — SimulatedPaymentProvider always succeeds by construction; there is no gateway to decline. Kept as an orphan node, not deleted.

nodes.label: [N/A UNDER DEC-010] Network failure at order submission
regions: no-false-success / no-duplicate-order guarantee on reconnect (preserved spec, not built)
nodes.note: Original AC-2.9, retired — order creation is a local SwiftData write with no network round-trip. What replaces it (atomic local write of Booking+PaymentRecord) is a general SwiftData-correctness concern, not a booking-flow branch — not modeled here.

flows.stack: push, depth 3+ (over HYP-002; also reachable directly from the inline Book-Now sheet at depth 2)
flows.trigger: Leisure Booker (or Guest-Checkout Booker) taps "Book Now" from the detail page or results list. Payment (or free/offline order) completes.
flows.bet: A flat, single-screen native checkout with a deliberately-chosen (not silently-inherited) guest-vs-account policy increases completed-booking rate
notes: Behavior only, per DEC-019. AC ids (AC-2.x) are the Given/When/Then criteria sharpened in reviews/ba-requirements-review.md § 3.2, plus one new AC (AC-2.11) authored in this pass to give the single-hotel-cart conflict interaction (DEC-008) a citable id — it had concrete, decision-backed UX copy but had never been numbered as an acceptance criterion (§ 4 Findings).

flows.title: Flow map — HYP-005: Primary Bookings tab

transitions.trigger: fetch succeeds, at least one booking

decision.question: What does the local SwiftData fetch for this guest's bookings return?

nodes.label: Bookings List
regions: Upcoming section — check-out date >= today, sorted soonest check-in first
Past section — check-out date < today, sorted most recent stay first
due-amount indicator inline per row (not detail-only)
nodes.note: Segmentation into Upcoming/Past (AC-3.2) is a BA recommendation, not a reference-derived fact — flagged as such in ba-requirements-review.md § 3.3 and repeated here since it's the one AC in this flow that's a proposal, not a settled requirement.

nodes.label: Empty Bookings
regions: explicit zero-bookings message (not a blank screen, not a perpetual spinner)

nodes.label: Data-Load Failure
regions: retry-capable error message, visually/textually distinct from node 2's zero-bookings message

nodes.label: [N/A UNDER DEC-010] Offline/cached viewing
nodes.note: AC-3.6, preserved not deleted. Not reachable — reservation detail is always a direct local SwiftData read, always current by definition; there is no cache/staleness distinction to surface. Shown as a disconnected/orphan node, exactly as ba-requirements-review.md marks it.

entered_from: app launch / tab bar (Bookings tab, always present)
flows.trigger: A registered guest opens the app to check on an upcoming stay or review a past one.
flows.bet: A primary 'Bookings' tab (not a tile-grid account dashboard) reduces time-to-find-next-trip and increases repeat app opens
notes: Behavior only, per DEC-019. AC ids (AC-3.x) are the Given/When/Then criteria sharpened in reviews/ba-requirements-review.md § 3.3. This is the smallest of the five flows.

flows.title: Flow map — HYP-006: Per-room cancellation with refund estimate

nodes.label: Cancellation Request
regions: per-room/line list, scoped to this booking — lines already checked-in/out or carrying an existing pending request are shown disabled with a reason (ineligible), the rest selectable (AC-5.1)
computed refund estimate, recalculated as line selection changes (AC-5.3)

transitions.trigger: guest selects at least one eligible line and taps Submit

nodes.note: Reachable identically regardless of persona (returning-guest or guest-checkout-booker) — no persona-based gate exists here, which is itself the requirement (AC-5.6, DEC-007 as collapsed by DEC-010). Drawn as a single entry arrow rather than two converging arrows, because showing a fork-then-merge would visually imply a distinction that the AC specifically says does not exist.

decision.question: Did the guest provide a required cancellation reason?

nodes.label: Cancellation Submitted
regions: "Cancellation request submitted — status: Pending" — copy must never imply an instant cancellation or an instant refund (AC-5.7, cross-cutting copy requirement, see § 3 Findings)
Done / back to Reservation Detail action

transitions.ac: AC-5.5 (part 1 — a CancellationRequest is created, status pending)

nodes.label: Status resolves

transitions.trigger: the local CancellationRequest state transitions from pending to resolved

nodes.note: Not a screen — a local state transition, timed independently of guest interaction (the demo's equivalent of the reference's staff-processed resolution). No UI is owned by this node; it exists to anchor the notification trigger.

nodes.label: Local Notification fires
nodes.note: A locally-scheduled UNUserNotificationCenter notification (DEC-013), not an app screen — no archetype/regions apply. Tapping it deep-links to the Reservation Detail screen (HYP-005 node 4) showing the resolved status.

flows.trigger: A registered guest, viewing a reservation, needs to cancel a room or a service line. As of DEC-007 (2026-08-13), this journey also serves a guest-checkout booker — the same submission mechanism below applies to both, unconditionally, with no channel distinction (DEC-007's original "on-device vs. cross-device" split collapsed under DEC-010's fully-local scope — see journeys/manage-reservations-guest.md). Only the entry point differs cosmetically (account dashboard vs. Bookings tab row), not the mechanism or the guest's capability.
flows.bet: Per-room cancellation requests with push-notified status updates and upfront policy display reduce cancellation-related support contact and guest anxiety

composition.title: Flow map — App composition: how the five flows join into one app

flows.label: Native Search & Discovery
entry_points: HYP-003 node 8, Continue Browsing (pop to root)
HYP-003 node 2.1 / node 0.1, empty-cart or cart-conflict-cancel (pop to root)
HYP-005 node 2, zero-bookings empty state (tab switch)
exit_points: -> HYP-002 node 8 (inline sheet), tap Book Now on a result card (sheet)

flows.label: Live Room Detail & Availability
entry_points: HYP-002 node 8.2/8.3 (sheet), guest opens full detail to resolve an unavailable/insufficient inline check (push)
HYP-003 node 0.1, Cart Conflict dialog cancelled (dismiss, returns to whichever screen triggered add-to-cart)

flows.label: Checkout & Simulated Payment
flows.stack_position: push, depth 3+ (over HYP-002; also reachable directly from the inline Book-Now sheet at depth 2)
entry_points: HYP-002 node 8.1, inline Book-Now check resolves available (push, skips Room Detail)
exit_points: -> HYP-005 node 0, Confirmation 'View My Bookings' (tab switch, Search stack reset to root)
-> HYP-001 node 0, Confirmation 'Continue Browsing' or empty-cart 'back to search' (pop to root)
-> HYP-001 node 2, Cart 'Continue Shopping' (pop one level)

flows.label: Primary Bookings Tab
entry_points: app launch / tab bar tap (always present, AC-3.1)
HYP-003 node 8, Confirmation 'View My Bookings' (tab switch)
HYP-006 node 4, local notification tapped (tab switch if needed, deep-link push to Reservation Detail)
exit_points: -> HYP-001 node 0, zero-bookings empty state 'back to search' (tab switch)

flows.label: Cancellation & Refund Estimate
entry_points: HYP-005 node 4, Reservation Detail 'Request Cancellation' (push) — identical entry for returning-guest and guest-checkout-booker, AC-5.6
exit_points: -> HYP-005 node 4, local notification tapped (deep-link push, may include a tab switch if the guest was elsewhere)

scope: Behavior only, per DEC-019: tab structure, what's a push vs. a sheet, where each flow is entered and exited, and where they hand off to each other. This is the piece the screen designs (ios-dev, docs/design/) hang on — no layout, no MD3 tokens, no visual hierarchy. Per DEC-018, native structural conventions (tab bar, nav stack, sheets) are platform-owned regardless of the MD3 surface styling ios-dev applies on top.

composition_note: Two tabs, no more — nothing in the promoted set covers an account or profile surface, so inventing one would be designing past the requirements.

findings.title: HYP-003 AC-2.5 — “Sign in instead”
findings.body: Names an option with no destination anywhere in the backlog. No authentication surface is in scope, so the control leads nowhere. Confirmed twice — once against the flow, once against the composition map.

findings.title: HYP-001 success metric
findings.body: A cross-session usage statistic. Real, but not a behaviour with a screen — nothing to draw.

findings.title: HYP-006 AC-5.7 — refund copy
findings.body: A cross-cutting wording requirement, not a branch. Applies across the cancellation flow rather than at any one node.

findings.title: Reference auto-refund branch
findings.body: QloApps refunds automatically when nothing was collected. Never carried into HYP-006’s criteria, and unclear whether it is reachable when payment always succeeds by construction (DEC-011).

findings.title: Notification deep-link needs a tab switch
findings.body: Tapping a cancellation notification may have to switch tabs before it can deep-link. Invisible from inside either HYP-005 or HYP-006 alone — only the composition map surfaced it.

findings.title: Cart conflict had copy but no criterion
findings.body: DEC-008’s “clear cart and add this instead?” interaction was specified in prose and never given an id. Now AC-2.11.

findings.title: HYP-001 and HYP-006 were never sharpened
findings.body: Both sat as prose bullets until this pass. They now carry explicit criteria — AC-4.1–4.5 and AC-5.1–5.7.

findings.title: AC-1.9 left a state undefined
findings.body: The inline Book Now check never said how it treats zero availability versus insufficient quantity. Extended by inference from AC-1.7/1.8, and flagged as inference rather than asserted.

findings.title: AC-1.5 minimum stay stays open
findings.body: Drawn as two live branches rather than resolved. Choosing between them is a tech-lead call.
